'Just like any other game': Pole remains humble ahead of 100 milestone
He’s the quiet, humble, respectful prop with the big smile who just goes about his business with minimal fuss.
It’s why Fonua Pole prefers to view his 100th NRL game this Saturday night as ‘just another game’, rather than being the one in the spotlight ahead of the Wests Tigers clash with the Nth Qld Cowboys in Townsville.
At just 24, Pole is in his fifth season in the NRL after making his debut for Wests Tigers at lock against the Warriors in July, 2022.
The New Zealand-born Tongan came through the Wests Tigers Pathways.
“I kind of don’t know how to feel right now. I keep trying to play it off, but I think it means more to my family’,’’ Pole said when asked about the milestone.
“They keep reminding me about how special it is. Just thinking back over the season and thinking about getting that debut, it was a special moment for me.
“Hundred games is crazy, especially how fast it went as well. I’m just grateful. I will treat it just like any other game.”
The match against the Cowboys also sees Pole reach 23 games in a season for the third time in five years which is testament to his hard work, preparation, durability, toughness, and commitment to succeed.
Those qualities are just many that team-mates like hooker and captain Api Korisau, and full-back Jahream Bula, admire about Pole.
“Fonua is one of the most impressive guys I've seen him and one of the most professional and humble young men that I've met,’’ Koroisau said.
“Just watching the way he goes about his work, he is in here every day doing recovery and developing his craft.
“I think the way he's played this year has really shown that as well. He's been one of our better players.
“Every week he turns up with the right attitude and really has a crack.
“You can work really hard off the field but for him to actually execute and play so well week in, week out and be one of our best players, is quite impressive."
Passion...Fonua Pole celebrates his try against Parramatta Eels with Api Koroisau ©NRL Imagery
Bula said he has developed a close friendship with Pole, with the pair sharing similar values.
“The way he carries himself off the field is one of the most impressive things for me,’’ Bula said.
“I think the way he is off the field translates onto the field as well.
“Fonua is very professional. He is always in doing recovery and extras, and it shows on the field.
Brothers in arms...Fonua Pole and Jahream Bula share a close friendship ©NRL Imagery
“He's a great player. He has been one of our better players this year. He has been killing it for us lately.”

August 27 th 2026, 1:19pm , By: Scooby
The concluding game on NRL Super Saturday heads to Townsville this week with the Cowboys hosting the Tigers . This is anything but a meaningless fixture as it promises to deliver an exciting rugby league contest. The Cowboys need a win in this game to keep their Finals hopes alive while the Tigers will want to put together a consecutive victory in a tough road trip.
Scooby is back with his preview and NRL tips for the Cowboys vs Tigers !
If you're looking for somewhere new to bet on the NRL, then help support our site by clicking on the banner below to join Neds ! They are one of Australia's best sportsbooks to bet on the NRL. Find out more in our Neds review .
Cowboys vs Tigers Prediction & Tips: 2026 NRL Round 26
Another week of pain
The Cowboys had the week off last week to lament their poor 32-30 loss on the road to the Eels in Round 24. As heavy favourites, the Cowboys failed to shut their opponents out of the match and kept the Finals hopes of teams around them alive. With 48% possession and an 84% completion rate, they ran for 9.5m per carry, made 622 PCM’s, but were let down defensively. They conceded 7 line breaks and missed 33 tackles, reflecting a lack of quality attitude which is needed for teams which have hopes of progressing far into the Finals series.
The upset of the year
A spirited 25-24 performance which caused the upset of the year for the Tigers over the Roosters provides hopes that this team is heading in the right direction. Entitled to collapse against a superior team, the Tigers squad did the opposite. They were competitive and played with poise (50% possession & 82% completion rate), overcoming plenty of setbacks over 80 minutes. Making 8.3m per carry, they created only 4 line breaks (Roosters 9) and missed 43 tackles. Yet, this mattered little as they sealed the victory with a last-gasp field goal to keep the hopes of an improved 2027 alive (for now).
Stats that matter
- The Tigers were victorious 44-16 against the Cowboys, making it their only victory in the past 5 games against the Cowboys. They also struggle on the road against this opponent, winning just 20% of matches. The Cowboys have a 54% strike rate at home.
- Despite only 2 of the past 5 games being decided by 6 points or less, the average margin of victory is still 14 points. They’re extremely high scoring contests too, with the average total sitting at 64 points.
- The Cowboys are far superior on both sides of the ball in 2026. They average 23ppg in attack but concede 26ppg defensively. While that is poor, it is still better than the Tigers, who score just 19ppg and allow 28ppg.
Fatigue to play a large role
The positive result which the Tigers enjoyed last week must be quickly forgotten as they prepare for this clash. Facing a team that is coming off a Bye, they will be fresh in tough conditions for the visitors. The lack of preparation time for the Tigers may cause them issues. The home team receives a huge boost with both Dearden and Nanai returning to their team. Their presence on the field offers the Cowboys stability and precision in their attack. The Tigers will struggle in the middle to handle the Cowboys speed and power, further impacted by the omission of Twal. Despite recording a victory over them already this season, the fortunes of each team ahead of this game are vastly different from earlier in the year. The Cowboys are prone to poor performances but with their season on the line, with key players returning, and playing at home, we should see a dominant display that solidifies their position in the Top 8 ahead of the concluding week of the regular season. As for a margin, expect the home team to make a statement; this will be a tight contest to begin with the Tigers riding high on the emotion from last week but in the end, the home team should pull away from them comfortably.

items.title: Curtains to draw on Cowboys star’s NRL career after cruel injury blow - Zero Tackle
items.snippet: Curtains to draw on Cowboys star’s NRL career after cruel injury blow    Zero Tackle
items.body_excerpt:
Murray Taulagi may have played his final NRL game, with the Queensland winger ruled out for the remainder of the season following another concussion.
Taulagi suffered his third concussion of 2026 after copping a head knock at training, with an independent doctor subsequently standing him down for six weeks.
The latest setback means the North Queensland Cowboys winger will not feature again this season, bringing his time with the club to an unfortunate end as he is set to join Rugby in France .
“He's seen the independent doctor, and he's stood down for six weeks,” Payten said.
“It's really disappointing, heartbreaking for him to finish that way with the club. I think everyone's taken it pretty hard initially, but it's important that what he does with the club for the next little period, he finishes on a good note within the building.
“Everyone's disappointed for him, and he'll be sadly missed.”
TOWNSVILLE, AUSTRALIA - MAY 28: Murray Taulagi of the Cowboys scores a try during the round 12 NRL match between the North Queensland Cowboys and the New Zealand Warriors at QCB Stadium, on May 28, 2021, in Townsville, Australia. (Photo by Ian Hitchcock/Getty Images)
Taulagi's NRL future was already set to take him away from Townsville, with the 26-year-old opting for a cross-code switch to French Rugby in 2027.
He had been heavily linked with a move to the Sydney Roosters , with his management initially giving the Cowboys an indication that he would remain in the NRL .
However, those plans ultimately changed, with Taulagi now set to continue his career in Europe.
“He's a real bubbly, infectious, important part of our team and I'm going to miss his cheek. He's got an opportunity overseas playing rugby in France , and I think he's very excited about that,” Payten said.
“The initial parts of our discussions, everything was indicating that he was going to go to a Sydney club, and through rumour and innuendo we sort of asked his management, ‘we kind of need to know so other options don't dry up'.
“They were clear and honest with us, and as things worked out, it didn't end up the way that they told us. So that's what happened, and we've moved on and signed a couple of players. Disappointing that he's not here, but he's in good hands.”
MELBOURNE, AUSTRALIA - SEPTEMBER 26: Sione Katoa of the Sharks is tackled by Cameron Munster of the Storm during the NRL Preliminary Final match between the Melbourne Storm and Cronulla Sharks at AAMI Park on September 26, 2025, in Melbourne, Australia. (Photo by Darrian Traynor/Getty Images)
Payten was referring to the double signing of Sharks winger Sione Katoa and centre Jesse Ramien , who will both make the move to Townsville next season on two-year contracts.
While the Cowboys had already moved to fill the void for next season, Taulagi's third concussion will bring an abrupt end to a seven-year career with the club.
The 26-year-old made his NRL debut for North Queensland in 2019 and has remained in Townsville ever since, going on to establish himself as a regular first-grade winger and Queensland Maroons representative on six occasions.

items.title: Joey’s major concern for Roosters in ‘make or break’ clash - Nine.com.au
items.snippet: Joey’s major concern for Roosters in ‘make or break’ clash    Nine.com.au
items.body_excerpt:
Andrew Johns has raised question marks over the Sydney Roosters ′ premiership credentials ahead of their “make or break” clash with the Dolphins .
After climbing to the top of the NRL ladder a fortnight ago with a gritty win over Penrith , things have unravelled slightly for the boys from Bondi.
Roosters halfback Sam Walker. Getty Images
In one of the biggest upsets of the year, the Roosters went down 25-24 to the struggling Wests Tigers , which saw them slide to third on the table.
Trent Robinson ’s men face an incredibly tough final two games of the regular season, first against the dangerous Dolphins before a round 27 showdown with local rivals South Sydney, who are expected to have Latrell Mitchell back.
Speaking on Wide World of Sports’ Immortal Behaviour to preview the Saturday evening blockbuster, Johns conceded that a loss to the Dolphins could result in the Roosters dropping out of the top-four and dashing their title hopes.
“It’s make or break for both, it’s so important for both these teams and I think more for the Roosters,” the rugby league Immortal said.
“I wouldn’t say it’s their biggest game of the year, but it’s the one with the biggest implications. They don’t wanna lose going into the last round against Souths.
Read more
‘A big thing’: Bennett reveals how ‘special’ Arrow plan was hatched
“If the Roosters lose [to the Dolphins], they can drop out of the four. This game has got huge implications, and you can’t win outside the top four, no team has done it and there’s a reason for that because it’s too hard.
“You look at that game against the Panthers and do you say it took it out of them? We’re gonna see where they’re at this weekend. If they lose, wow - it puts so much pressure on them going into that game against South Sydney.
“If the Roosters lose, I think they’ll miss the top four.”
As it stands, the Roosters are on 38 competition points – one win ahead of the Dolphins and two wins ahead of Cronulla – but two losses in the final two weeks would likely see them slip to fifth on the ladder due to points differential.
On the flip side, a victory for the Dolphins over one of the NRL heavyweights could hold them in good stead heading into their maiden finals campaign.
“They’re a big chance and if you get them in the semis and they catch fire, no one is beating them,” Johns said.
“If they beat the Roosters, I say they are a genuine chance.”
Johns believes the strike power in the Dolphins’ backline, led by the likes of Herbie Farnworth and Hamiso Tabuai-Fidow , could cause issues for the Tricolours.
Herbie Farnworth has cemented himself as the NRL’s best centre. Getty Images
He also pointed to the defensive issues on both of the Roosters’ edges as an area the Dolphins could look to expose, while labelling the absence of Victor Radley as a “really big out” after he was concussed against the Tigers.
The highly-anticipated match between the Roosters and Dolphins kicks off at 5.30pm on Saturday evening at Allianz Stadium.
